chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he

he had a wife who astounded him and he loved her. So one morning he had divorced her, and was grieved because of that. So one of his companions said to him: 'May I be your ransom! Why did you divorce her?' So he said: 'Indeed I mentioned Ali (peace be upon him), and she belittled him. So I disliked that I should press an ember from the embers of Hell to my skin.'

key_terms.تَنَقَّصَتْهُ: She belittled/diminished him — she spoke disrespectfully of Imam Ali
key_terms.جَمْرَةٌ مِنْ جَمْرِ جَهَنَّمَ: An ember from the embers of Hell — a metaphor for the spiritual harm of associating with enemies of the Imams
key_terms.مَوَالِي: Mawali — clients, freedmen, or close companions attached to a household

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir divorce his beloved wife according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) divorced a wife he loved dearly after she spoke disparagingly of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). When asked why, he explained using a vivid metaphor: keeping her would be like pressing a burning coal from Hellfire against his own skin — meaning that associating with someone who disrespects the Imams is a spiritual danger that no worldly attachment can justify. This hadith is found in the chapter on divorcing an incompatible woman, and demonstrates that religious and spiritual incompatibility — especially hostility toward the Ahlulbayt — constitutes sufficient grounds for divorce in Shia jurisprudence.
